article_title: Influence of Meta-Cognitive Training and Cognitive Styles on Numeracy Achievement of Nigerian Pupils' in Computer-Mediated Classrooms
citation: Taiwo Oladunni Gbenga-Akanmu & Philip Olu Jegede. (2019). Influence of Meta-cognitive Training and Cognitive Styles on Numeracy Achievement of Nigerian Pupils’ in Computer-mediated Classrooms. World Journal of Education, 9(1). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v9n1p221
title: Computer Numeracy Instructional Package for Primary School Children (CNIP 2SC)
description: CNIP 2SC is a computer-mediated instructional package developed by the researchers to teach primary school numeracy concepts. It was built "alongside with the scheme of work from the schools" and provided "the blueprint for teaching numeracy concepts (Numbers and Numeration, Basic Operations and Measurement)". It contained series of exercises pupils worked on, with the researcher serving as teacher/facilitator; it was used to teach both experimental and control groups for six weeks.
requirements: Computer facilities available in the schools, which was the basis for purposive school selection
constraints: Used with primary three pupils in two Nigerian schools; the chalk method was not used, teaching was done using computers
target_learning_goals: numeracy concepts: Number and Numeration, Basic Operations, and Measurement
examples: Both experimental and control groups were taught numeracy with CNIP 2SC for six weeks before post-testing with PATON
key_sources: Taiwo Oladunni Gbenga-Akanmu & Philip Olu Jegede. (2019). Influence of Meta-cognitive Training and Cognitive Styles on Numeracy Achievement of Nigerian Pupils’ in Computer-mediated Classrooms. World Journal of Education, 9(1). https://doi.org/10.5430/wje.v9n1p221

article_title: Large Language Model Performance on Multistep Clinical Cases: Comparative Study Across Question and Case Levels.
citation: Cha J, Zhao Y, Zong H. (2026). Large Language Model Performance on Multistep Clinical Cases: Comparative Study Across Question and Case Levels. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/95342
title: Curated dataset of 189 multistep clinical cases (473 questions) from the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination
description: The study curated a benchmark of sequential case-based questions from the CNMLE covering 2017 to 2021, screened in three steps to 189 unique clinical cases comprising 473 individual questions. A physician with more than 8 years of clinical experience annotated the cases, confirming that "82.5% (156/189) contained sequentially dependent questions." Cases contain 2 to 4 questions each covering stages of clinical management within a shared patient vignette.
requirements: Cases were restricted to sequential case-based questions with specific patient demographic or clinical information
constraints: Text-based multiple-choice questions only; cases requiring interpretation of medical images were not included
The study was conducted only in Chinese
target_learning_goals: evaluating LLM performance on multistep clinical reasoning tasks
examples: 53.4% (n=101) of cases contained 2 questions, 42.9% (n=81) contained 3, and 3.7% (n=7) contained 4
key_sources: Cha J, Zhao Y, Zong H. (2026). Large Language Model Performance on Multistep Clinical Cases: Comparative Study Across Question and Case Levels. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/95342

article_title: Artificial intelligence-based action recognition and skill assessment in robotic cardiac surgery simulation: a feasibility study.
citation: Atroshchenko Gennady V., Korup Lærke Riis, Hashemi Nasseh, Østergaard Lasse Riis, Tolsgaard Martin G., Rasmussen Sten. (2025). Artificial intelligence-based action recognition and skill assessment in robotic cardiac surgery simulation: a feasibility study. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-025-02563-3
title: CNN-LSTM architecture combining spatial feature extraction with temporal modeling for surgical video analysis
description: The article's model combines a Convolutional Neural Network for extracting spatial features with a Long Short-Term Memory layer to incorporate temporal information. The input passes through four convolutional layers with pooling, is flattened into the LSTM, and a dense layer outputs two probabilities (suturing or dissection; expert or novice). The authors argue the LSTM "enables the model to recognize patterns over time rather than just isolated frames", enabling granular, moment-by-moment assessment and moving toward real-time skill assessment. Dropout of 0.20, batch normalization, and L2 regularization of 0.01 were applied to mitigate overfitting.
requirements: Regularization techniques (dropout 0.20, batch normalization, L2 regularization 0.01) to mitigate overfitting given limited data
constraints: Developed and tested only on robotic cardiac surgery wet lab tasks; further testing is needed to determine generalizability to unseen videos from different surgeons
target_learners: surgeons in robotic cardiac surgery simulation training
target_learning_goals: automated post-procedural assessment and feedback on surgical performance
examples: Shorter five-frame sequences were used for action recognition while 10-second sequences were chosen for skill assessment
